providers.market_view: The German market is attempting a recovery following a period of intense selling pressure. Investor sentiment is stabilizing as a multi-day losing streak appears to have broken, driven by a rebound in technology and industrial sectors. While broad indices have reclaimed key psychological levels, the environment remains sensitive to individual earnings revisions and idiosyncratic risks. Sector rotation is visible, with capital moving back into high-beta technology and renewable energy names, while traditional automotive and some commodity-related stocks continue to face downward momentum or technical breakdowns.

German equities enter the cutoff after a forceful broad rebound from a weak week, raising consolidation risk for index beta and Monday's biggest winners. With US liquidity thinning into Thanksgiving and macro event risk later in the week, I prefer liquid DAX ordinaries whose own corporate events fall inside the five-session window and whose shares lagged the rebound. The focus is company-specific re-rating potential in chemicals and reinsurance, not defense, autos or rate-sensitive sector beta.

# BASF raises profit forecast; cost-cutting measures to continue until 2029
...
The German chemicals group BASF posted a significantly higher operating profit in the third quarter of 2026 thanks to higher prices and lower fixed costs, and has revised its full-year forecast upwards. However, according to CEO Markus Kamieth, cost-cutting and job cuts are far from over. ‘From now until 2028 or 2029, you will continue to see significant restructuring and job cuts,’ he said on Wednesday during the presentation of the quarterly report.

# Basf Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
...
Third-quarter performance improved: EBITDA before special items rose 15% year over year to €1.6 billion, driven by price increases, volume growth, stronger margins and lower fixed costs across all four core businesses.

2026 outlook was modestly raised: BASF now expects EBITDA before special items of €7.4 billion–€7.8 billion, while maintaining its free-cash-flow forecast of €1.5 billion–€2.3 billion amid continued geopolitical and energy-market uncertainty.

Capital discipline and portfolio actions continued: BASF reduced net debt by 20% year over year, lowered its capital-expenditure forecast, repurchased about €1.9 billion of shares and said Agricultural Solutions remains on track to be IPO-ready by mid-2027.
